clue.text: Like the origin of all solutions here, maybe a pure one

definitions.text: Like the origin of all solutions here

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters of the phrase that follows are only one possible arrangement, so they are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A puzzle-maker remarks that every answer comes from the same place, and a 'pure one' at that.
explanation.walkthrough: Every answer in this grid is a word or phrase borrowed from a language of the continent, which is what the definition points to.
explanation.definitionFit: Every solution in the grid is a loanword from a continental language such as French, German, Italian or Latin.

clue.text: Endless protest in capital

indicators.note: Endless says the word for the protest loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a go-slow is a form of industrial protest in which workers deliberately slow down

explanation.surface: A protest that never seems to stop, staged in a nation's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' strips G and W from GOSLOW.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian city is that country's seat of government, an example of a capital.

clue.text: Sexually fluid reporter not half cross to get trinkets

parts.note: bisexual, shortened to bi, describes attraction to more than one sex

indicators.note: not half keeps only the first half of the word for the reporter

parts.note: a journo is an informal word for a journalist or reporter
an X is a cross-shaped mark

explanation.surface: A journalist of fluid sexuality grows annoyed while acquiring some baubles.
explanation.definitionFit: Bijoux is the French plural for jewels, used in English for small ornaments or knick-knacks.

clue.text: Player's instruction is a grunt, rubbish on ball

parts.note: a grunt is US slang for an infantry soldier, a GI
tat is cheap rubbishy goods
the letter O is round like a ball

explanation.surface: A musician complains that a direction amounts to a grunt and nonsense about a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian musical direction tells a performer to play in an agitated, restless manner.

clue.text: Officer, almost 51, about to provide pottery

indicators.note: almost says the officer's word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: a major is an army officer
LI is 51 in Roman numerals
ca, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A nearly 51-year-old officer is on the point of supplying some ceramics.
explanation.definitionFit: Majolica is a kind of tin-glazed earthenware originally from Italy, so a type of pottery.

clue.text: French writing experts start from bad track records

indicators.note: start from takes just the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: a rail is a track for trains
lists are records of items

explanation.surface: Specialists in French handwriting begin their work from poor railway records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' looks like the language; the tactile script is named after the Frenchman Louis Braille.
explanation.definitionFit: People skilled in the raised-dot reading system devised by the Frenchman Louis Braille are its expert practitioners.

clue.text: Note fake news for all to see in context

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
a lie is false information, fake news
U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for universal viewing

explanation.surface: A note puts fake news on public display, framed in its proper context.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's milieu is their social setting or surroundings, the context in which they live.

clue.text: Traitor in Paris who has basic weapon

parts.note: qui is French for who
a sling is a simple missile-throwing weapon

explanation.surface: A turncoat in the French capital is equipped with a primitive weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Vidkun Quisling collaborated with the Nazis in Norway, and his name became a byword for a collaborator.

clue.text: Not all in bureau re-invested coins

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some, but not every, coin in a bureau has been put back into investment.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'bureau' into 're-invested'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aurei were gold pieces of ancient Rome, the plural of aureus, so they are coins.

clue.text: Can containing one hundred bananas

indicators.note: containing says the toilet word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: can is slang for a toilet, as is loo
C is the Roman numeral for one hundred

explanation.surface: A tin holds a hundred bananas.
explanation.definitionFit: Loco is slang for crazy, as is bananas, both meaning mad.

clue.text: Sixties' approach of westerners in pool: sit with kit off

indicators.note: off says these words go wrong, so their letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Visitors from the west at a swimming pool are told to sit with their gear removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' is the anagram signal; the 'westerners' of the definition are West Germans, whose government pursued this eastward policy.
explanation.definitionFit: This German term names West Germany's 1960s policy of opening relations with the Eastern bloc.

clue.text: Met radical in Congress, which is explosive

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters inside the word for congress

parts.note: congress is a formal word for sexual intercourse

indicators.note: radical suggests drastic change, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A radical encountered in the US Congress proves politically explosive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'radical' makes TEM, and 'in' places it within the word for sexual congress.
explanation.definitionFit: Semtex is a plastic explosive made in the Czech Republic.

clue.text: Film screened by Lean, director with odd post-war story

indicators.note: screened by says the film sits inside the next word, as if hidden behind it

parts.note: lean means thin
ET is Spielberg's film about an extraterrestrial
rum is an old-fashioned word for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A film shown by David Lean, director of a peculiar story set after the war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lean' looks like the director David Lean but just means THIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Günter Grass's 1959 novel, set around the Second World War and its aftermath, is a post-war German story.

clue.text: Follow fashion rule in women's clothing

parts.note: to tail someone is to follow them

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape, so the letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone keeps up with fashion's rules when it comes to dressing women.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailleur is a French-style tailored suit for women, an item of their dress.

clue.text: Italian footballers spoke vacuously amongst themselves

parts.note: Inter Milan is a famous Italian football club

indicators.note: vacuously says the word is emptied of its middle, keeping only the outer letters

explanation.surface: Players from an Italian club chatted idly with one another.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin phrase means between or among the parties themselves, used of private dealings.

clue.text: Performed musical works without opening drinks

parts.note: sang means performed a song

indicators.note: without opening says the word for the songs loses its first letter

parts.note: arias are solo songs in operas

explanation.surface: Singers performed pieces of music without first having a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Sangria is a Spanish punch of red wine and fruit, so these are drinks.

clue.text: Plague overtakes woman, one likely to wail

indicators.note: overtakes is read as taking the woman over, so she is swallowed inside the curse word

parts.note: a bane is a curse or plague
she refers to a woman

explanation.surface: An epidemic catches up with a woman, who will probably cry out.
explanation.definitionFit: In Irish folklore this female spirit wails to warn of an approaching death.

clue.text: Lose rent rebuilding mezzanine

indicators.note: rebuilding says the letters are taken apart and put together in a different order

explanation.surface: A landlord forfeits rent while the mezzanine floor is reconstructed.
explanation.definitionFit: An entresol is a low storey between the ground and first floors, the same as a mezzanine.

clue.text: Kind of complex reference work, one on China

parts.note: the OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
I is the Roman numeral for one
pal means mate, and china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate)

explanation.surface: A complicated kind of reference book, the sort that discusses porcelain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like porcelain or the country; in Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate, so a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: Freud's Oedipus complex is a psychological complex, and the adjective describes it.

clue.text: West African church lacks good atmosphere

indicators.note: lacks says a letter is missing from what precedes it

parts.note: a Gambian comes from the Gambia in West Africa
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A West African church is missing a pleasant atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambiance is the mood or character a place has, its atmosphere.

clue.text: Sweet pout, maintaining smiles on the outside

indicators.note: maintaining means holding, so the pout word holds the next letters inside it

parts.note: a moue is a pouting expression

indicators.note: on the outside picks the outer letters of the word

explanation.surface: A cute pout hides behind a smiling face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the outside' takes the first and last letters of 'smiles', and 'maintaining' holds that pair within the pout word.
explanation.definitionFit: A mousse is a light, frothy dessert, which in Britain is called a sweet.

clue.text: Appropriately placed university not very funny

indicators.note: not says the letters of the following word are taken away from the pool
funny suggests the letters are behaving oddly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A university that isn't especially amusing is in the right place.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of VERY out of UNIVERSITY ('not') and rearrange the rest ('funny').
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin phrase means in the original or proper position, so in its correct place.

clue.text: Enjoying popularity, like old colour

parts.note: something in is fashionable and popular
to dig something is slang for liking it

explanation.surface: Being popular, as an old colour might be.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is the deep blue dye and hue between blue and violet in the spectrum.

clue.text: Very successful young person with sub-species?

parts.note: sub as a prefix means under
a species is a kind

explanation.surface: A query about a brilliant youngster linked to a subspecies.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'sub-species' as two words: SUB is UNDER and SPECIES is KIND.
explanation.definitionFit: This German loanword means a wonder child, someone who achieves great success at a young age.

clue.text: Settler right behind City institution

indicators.note: behind places the letter for right after the institution

parts.note: the BoE is the Bank of England, in the City of London

explanation.surface: A colonist stands just behind a financial institution in the City.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: The Boers were Dutch-descended farmers who colonised southern Africa.

clue.text: Character's whisker, as some say?

indicators.note: as some say marks a pronunciation, as in non-rhotic accents that drop the final r

parts.note: a beater is a kitchen tool for whisking eggs or cream

explanation.surface: Someone's whiskers, at least according to some people.
explanation.walkthrough: In accents that drop a final R, BEATER is said like the Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a character.

clue.text: A Spanish female with appeal? This'll get hot

parts.note: SA stands for sex appeal
una is the feminine form of 'a' in Spanish

explanation.surface: A Spanish woman with sex appeal, the kind who will warm things up.
explanation.definitionFit: A sauna is a steam or dry-heat room that becomes very warm.

clue.text: Fear Gypsies dropping back a short distance

parts.note: angst is anxiety or dread

indicators.note: dropping back says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: the Roma are the Romani people, sometimes called Gypsies

explanation.surface: Fear of travellers who fall back only a little way.
explanation.definitionFit: An angstrom is a unit of length of one ten-billionth of a metre, a tiny distance.
